evidence: Homepage lists 6 templates (Professional Resume, Professional Email, Weekly Status Report, Meeting Minutes, Project Proposal, Academic Research Summary) each showing author name and description.

Each template card shows title (e.g. "Professional Resume"), author ("Sarah Chen"), description, category ("Resume"), scenario ("Business"), usage count ("1,250 uses"), and update date ("Updated 2024-12-01").
Clicking "Use Template" on Professional Resume opened a dialog showing template details (category, scenario, description, author, usage count) plus a "Fill Template" form with all field inputs.

With all fields empty, dialog shows "Required fields missing: Please fill in: Full Name, Job Title, Email, Professional Summary, Company Name, Position, Start Date, Responsibilities, Degree, School, Graduation Year, Skills" and the "Preview Result" tab is disabled.
All 13 fields (12 required + Phone optional) of the Professional Resume template accepted entered values.
After filling all required fields, "Preview Result" tab became enabled and clicking it rendered a formatted resume with all entered values substituted.

Preview shows h1 "Timothee Issenmann", bold job title, separator line, h2 sections (Professional Summary, Experience, Education, Skills), h3 company/position, italic date range, all placeholders replaced with entered values, no unresolved placeholders.
Preview tab was disabled while required fields were empty, and became enabled/populated only after all required fields received valid values.
Markdown template (Professional Resume) rendered proper Markdown (headings, bold, italic, separator) after field substitution in the Preview Result tab.
Clicking "Copy to Clipboard" produced a toast "Copied to clipboard! The generated content has been copied." and the button changed to "Copied!".

issue: No format validation for declared-format fields (e.g. email)
actual: Entering "not-an-email" into the required Email field of the Professional Resume template produced no validation error, and the Preview Result tab remained enabled and rendered the invalid value verbatim ("not-an-email") in the output instead of rejecting it or keeping the preview unavailable.

issue: Duplicate field labels are not rejected or disambiguated
actual: Adding a second field with the same label "note" (same generated placeholder key {{note}}) was accepted without any warning, error, or automatic disambiguation — the field list now shows two identical "note" fields both mapping to {{note}}.

evidence: Submitted a Markdown custom template "QA Quick Note" with title, description, author, category (Other default), scenario (Business default), content with {{fullname}} and {{note}} placeholders, and two defined fields (fullName required, note optional). Submission succeeded with toast "Template submitted! Your template has been added to the library."
Immediately after submission, without any page reload, the library count updated from "Showing 6 of 6 templates" to "Showing 7 of 7 templates" and a new "QA Quick Note" card appeared in the grid.
Clicking "Use Template" on the newly submitted "QA Quick Note" card opened its fill form, and filling required field "fullName" and optional "note" allowed generating a preview successfully.

Custom template defined fields fullName and note mapped exactly to content placeholders {{fullname}} and {{note}}; submission succeeded, and the generated preview substituted both placeholders fully with no unresolved {{...}} tokens remaining.

Entering special/markdown-breaking characters ("# Hacked\n\n**Bold Injection** | <script>alert(1)</script>") into a template field triggered inline validation error "Special characters like < > { } [ ] \\ | ` are not allowed" and disabled the Preview Result tab, preventing generation.

Attempting to submit the "Submit a Template" form with title, author, description, content, and fields all blank produced toast "Missing required fields — Please fill in all required fields." and the dialog remained open without submitting.

Typing "Res" showed real-time suggestions (Professional Resume, Responsibilities, In Progress, Academic Research Summary, Research Title) and narrowed results live to 4 of 7; clicking suggestion "Professional Resume" filled the search box with that text and narrowed results to 1 of 7 matching template.

issue: Search does not tolerate typos (no fuzzy matching)
actual: Searching "Propsal" (typo for "Proposal") and "Reusme" (typo for "Resume") both returned "Showing 0 of 7 templates" with "No templates found" and no suggestions, instead of returning/suggesting the intended template.

evidence: Category filter (e.g. "Resume") narrowed results to 1 of 7; Scenario filter (e.g. "Academic") narrowed to 1 of 7; Sort By offers Most Popular, Recently Updated, Oldest First, Alphabetical — selecting "Alphabetical" correctly reordered cards A-Z (Academic Research Summary, Meeting Minutes, Professional Email, Professional Resume, Project Proposal, QA Quick Note, Weekly Status Report). Default "Most Popular" correctly ordered by descending usage count (1250,1100,890,720,560,340,0).
Search, category filter, scenario filter, and sort selections all updated the visible result count and card order immediately without any page reload throughout testing.

Favoriting Professional Resume and Meeting Minutes updated the Favorites button count live (0→1→2). Clicking Favorites opened a favorites-only view showing exactly the 2 favorited cards ("Showing 2 of 7 templates"). Unfavoriting Professional Resume from within that view immediately removed it and updated count to 1.
Favorites button badge count updated instantly (1→2→1) on each favorite/unfavorite click, with the corresponding card appearing/disappearing from the favorites-only list without any page reload.

Within the favorites-only view (1 template favorited), typing "Meeting" produced live suggestions and correctly matched/narrowed to the favorited "Meeting Minutes" template ("Showing 1 of 7 templates"); clearing the search restored the favorites-only list with the card intact.

After a full page reload of http://localhost:6089/, the Favorites button still shows count "1" (Meeting Minutes remained favorited), and the custom "QA Quick Note" template submitted earlier is still present in the full template list (7 of 7 templates), confirming both favorites and custom templates persist across reload.
